cases.summary: The rider claims they were at the main entrance on time but was charged a no-show fee after the driver stopped far away and barely tried to reach them. The retrieved evidence, however, shows the driver met all three NS-1 conditions: closest approach 145 m (within the 150 m limit), waited 300 s within threshold (meeting the 300 s minimum), and made one recorded call attempt before cancelling. Under NS-1, the no-show fee is properly retained, and NS-2's refund trigger is not met. The rider's position is not supported by the current-trip evidence.

arguments.claim: The driver came within 150 m of the pickup point, satisfying the first NS-1 condition.
The driver waited the full 300 seconds from first coming within 150 m until cancelling, satisfying the second NS-1 condition.
The driver made at least one recorded contact attempt (a call) before cancelling, satisfying the third NS-1 condition.
Because all three NS-1 conditions are met, the no-show fee of S$5.00 is properly retained and no refund is owed.

cases.summary: The driver met every condition required to retain the no-show fee under NS-1. GPS telemetry shows the driver came within 145 m of the pickup pin (limit 150 m), waited the full 300 seconds from first entering the threshold until cancelling, and made a recorded call attempt before cancelling. The rider's claim that the driver 'stopped far away and barely tried to reach me' is contradicted by the computed pickup metrics and the call log. The no-show fee of S$5.00 should be retained.

result.reasoning: The no-show policy NS-1 requires three conditions to retain the fee: driver within 150 m of pickup, wait of at least 300 s from first entering the threshold until cancelling, and at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling. GPS-PICKUP shows a closest approach of 145 m (within the 150 m limit), a wait of 300 s (meeting the 300 s minimum), and CHAT-SUMMARY/CALL-01 show one recorded call attempt before cancellation. All three conditions are literally met, so NS-2's refund trigger is not activated. The rider's location claim in CHAT-01 is untrusted text and cannot override GPS metrics per NS-4, and party histories are context only. The remedy is keep_charge.
